text:
incident-bot: paging @sre-oncall :rotating_light: detected error spike on canary cluster during deploy (release/2026.3.15). 500s in /v1/generate, DB errors in logs mentioning 'column \"user_profile\" contains nulls' - possible non-null constraint added in migration. impact ~2% traffic.

sre-oncall: I'm on it, grabbing context. Which canary?

katie: canary is us-west-2a, release pinned to model-route v3 + migration 20260315_add_user_profile_notnull.sql. Canary traffic 5% initially.

db-admin: I see stuck migration job on writer-01: 
```\npg_migrate[pid=4212]: applying step 3/7: set user_profile not null\npsql: ERROR: could not create constraint because table contains null values\n```
Looks like the migration assumed a backfilled column but backfill failed/was skipped.

maria: did we backfill in advance? I remember a data backfill planned but not executed for low-latency path.

katie: backfill was scheduled as background job but we didn't run the long tail due to time. Ops thought to rely on default filler but that didn't happen.

incident-bot: created incident INC-2026-0315-01, severity: high. Paging escalation to oncall + db-admin.

sre-oncall: immediate plan: stop canary traffic / kill rollout, flip feature flag to stop writes that rely on new column, and see if we can rollback migration. Any objections?

deploy-bot: canary rollback queued: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/api-canary --to-revision=prev` (dry-run). Note: rollback will not automatically revert DB migration.

katie: do NOT run migration rollback yet. If migration partially applied and we revert code, we could hit null constraint errors on old code expecting nulls. Better to kill feature, stop traffic to canary, and surface customers.

product-ops: support: prepare banner draft. Affected endpoints intermittently returning 500 for small percentage of users. No data loss confirmed yet.

alex: attempted to run backfill on writer-01 but it's CPU-bound and taking very long. Backfill process shows many rows with nulls in user_profile. Suggest pausing writes that create new rows requiring this column.

sre-oncall: toggling feature flag 'require_user_profile' to OFF for canary + rollout groups now.

katie: feature flag toggled. Confirming write failures drop.

product-ops: support, send this to SLO channel: impact < 5% requests and errors spiking in canary tier only. No widespread outage.

db-admin: even with flag off, migration is still in partly-applied state (some tables altered). Attempting snapshot of current schema and creating an idempotent migration to make column nullable again if needed. Running `pg_dump --schema-only` for diff.

maria: any chance of rolling the migration back safely? Is there a reversible path?

db-admin: Not straightforward: ALTER TABLE ... DROP NOT NULL is cheap and reversible, but if other steps (index creation + data cleanup) happened, must validate. I can run `ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN user_profile DROP NOT NULL;` as emergency revert to unblock the API, then plan follow-up for proper backfill.

katie: go ahead with DROP NOT NULL on writer-01 but only after we ensure replicas are caught up. Coordinate window with SRE to avoid replication lag.

sre-oncall: checking replica lag across writer replicas. lag ~0-2s. Safe to apply.

db-admin: executing on writer-01: `BEGIN; ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN user_profile DROP NOT NULL; COMMIT;`

deploy-bot: noticed deploys paused. Canary rollback still pending; code report: clients now see reduced 500s.

alex: monitoring metrics: error rate on /v1/generate dropped from 7% to 0.6% in canary within 3m. Good.

maria: confirm no data loss and we didn't accidentally mutate actual user_profile values. We're only dropping constraint.

db-admin: confirmed: no rows changed by the DROP NOT NULL, just constraint removed. Backfill still needed for eventual stronger contract.

katie: next steps: (1) finish canary rollback of code to previous release (no DB migration applied), (2) mark migration as blocked and add gate to CI, (3) schedule controlled backfill with throttling and monitoring, (4) retrospective on migration runbook.

deploy-bot: rolling back canary now: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/api-canary --to-revision=12345` -> success, pods restarted.

incident-bot: deploy rollback action recorded.

product-ops: support message to customers: short blurb: \"We experienced an intermittent error affecting a small subset of API requests during a canary deployment. We've rolled back the canary and removed a database constraint to restore service. No user data was lost. We're investigating the root cause and will follow up.\"

tim: any impact to dedicated or private customers?

katie: no evidence beyond canary pool. Verified logs for dedicated clusters show no errors.

alex: creating a follow-up ticket with remediation checklist: `- add pre-flight backfill stage to deployment, - add CI guard preventing non-null constraint migrations without zero-null proof, - add migration dry-run that validates zero-null assumption on sampled data`

maria: thanks everyone. I'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow and include oncall rotation notes.

sre-oncall: handing off to next shift in 30m. Incident marked mitigated but needs follow-up. 

incident-bot: incident INC-2026-0315-01 status -> mitigated. Actions logged to INC board.

katie: closing thread for live ops, please update the incident ticket with timeline + remediation before EOD. :white_check_mark:
